source: Seven learning exchanges saved as one batch
lessonTheme: Yes/no questions, readiness recall and time meaning
summary: After saying Yo no sé and receiving a model, produced three structurally correct prompted yes/no questions. Correctly selected lo/la and listo/lista in this round. Esto for está recurred once; está was then recalled in the next two readiness statements. Omitted yet from a requested not-yet sentence, while ya was correctly used in a statement and question. Standard punctuation and accents supplied.

observations.outcome: Natural I don't know response, rather than an attempted question. Accent/capitalization supplied; No sé modelled as a natural shorter alternative. Tutor re-explained unchanged word order for the practised yes/no questions.
Correct question word order, readiness verb and masculine adjective immediately after explanation. Opening question mark, accent and capitalization supplied.
Correct can-use-it question and masculine lo for the stated logo referent; opening question mark supplied.

observations.learnerText: Si podemos usarlo porque esto listo
observations.correctedText: Sí, podemos usarlo porque está listo.
observations.outcome: Correct affirmative ability, object lo, porque and masculine listo. Recurrent esto for está corrected explicitly: está means it is here; esto means this. Sí accent supplied.

observations.learnerText: No podemos usarlo porque No esta listo
observations.correctedText: No podemos usarlo porque no está listo.
observations.outcome: Grammatical sentence with both negatives and correct object/agreement; está form recalled after immediate correction. Omitted requested yet, so tutor supplied No podemos usarlo porque todavía no está listo. Do not count this as successful recall of todavía.
Correct feminine agreement and natural sentence-final ya for ready now. Accents supplied. Alternative La función ya está lista modelled.

Correct question structure, feminine la for stated función referent and sentence-final ya. Opening question mark supplied. Three structurally correct prompted questions in this round; delayed retention remains untested.

nextSteps: Recheck todavía no with an unhinted familiar sentence
Review está versus esto after intervening material
Revisit earlier goals, purpose/reason and location vocabulary before adding more grammar
Keep question structure success separate from supplied opening question marks and accents
assessmentNote: All successful question uses were prompted in the same practice sequence after an explanation. No long-term retention or broad ser/estar mastery inferred.
